seoTitle: UART Baud Rate Divisor and Error Calculator
metaDescription: Find the baud rate register value for a microcontroller clock, the actual baud rate and the percentage error for 16x and 8x oversampling.
intro: Check whether your clock can produce a baud rate accurately, before you wonder why serial output is garbled.
why:
Enter the clock frequency and target baud rate. For normal (16x) and double-speed (8x) modes the page computes the exact divisor, the rounded register value (UBRR = round(f/(oversampling*baud)) - 1), the baud rate actually generated, the error percentage and a verdict (under about 2% is fine, around 3% is marginal).

Both ends need to agree within the UART tolerance, so errors on each side add up. Crystals such as 18.432 MHz and 3.6864 MHz divide evenly into standard baud rates.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Enter the clock in Hz and the baud rate.
Pick the register value with the smallest error.
Choose a different crystal if both are poor.

faq.a: Roughly under 2% in total between transmitter and receiver.
The AVR double-speed bit that halves the oversampling to 8x.
